title: Verb + to ... (decide to ... / forget to ... etc.)
subtitle: decide to ... / forget to ...
summary: Use to + infinitive after verbs like decide, agree, offer, refuse, manage, seem and pretend, and after a question word (how/what/where to ...).

lesson.heading: Verbs followed by to ...
lesson.text: After these verbs you can use **to ...** (infinitive): **offer, agree, refuse, decide, plan, arrange, hope, forget, manage, fail, promise, threaten, deserve, afford, learn, tend**.

examples.text: It was a long way to walk, so we **decided to take** a taxi home.
Simon was in a difficult situation, so I **agreed to help** him.
I waved to Karen, but **failed to attract** her attention.
I like Dan, but I think he **tends to talk** too much.
How old were you when you **learnt to drive**?

lesson.heading: The negative, and verbs that take -ing instead
lesson.text: The negative is **not to ...**. Remember that after some verbs we use -ing (not to ...), for example enjoy, think of and suggest.

examples.text: We decided **not to go** out because of the weather.
I promised **not to be** late.
I **enjoy reading**.
Andy **suggested meeting** for coffee.
Are you **thinking of buying** a car?

lesson.heading: dare
lesson.text: After **dare** you can use the infinitive with or without to. But after **dare not** (or **daren't**), we do not use to.

examples.text: I didn't **dare to tell** him.
examples.note: or I didn't dare tell him.

examples.text: I **daren't tell** him what happened.

lesson.heading: seem / appear / pretend / claim
lesson.text: We also use **to ...** after **seem, appear, pretend** and **claim**. You can also use **to be -ing** (continuous infinitive) and **to have (done)** (perfect infinitive).

examples.text: They **seem to have** plenty of money.
Ann **pretended not to see** me when she passed me in the street.
I **pretended to be reading** the newspaper.
examples.note: = I pretended that I was reading

examples.text: Have you seen my keys? I **seem to have lost** them.
examples.note: = it seems that I have lost them

examples.text: She **claimed not to have seen** me.
examples.note: = she claimed that she hadn't seen me

lesson.heading: Question word + to ...
lesson.text: After **ask, know, decide, remember, forget, learn, explain, understand** and **wonder** you can use a question word (what/how/where etc.) + to ... . You can also **show/tell/ask/advise/teach somebody what/how/where to do** something.

examples.text: We asked **how to get** to the station.
Have you decided **where to go** on holiday?
I don't know **whether to apply** for the job or not.
Can somebody show me **how to use** this camera?
Ask Jack. He'll tell you **what to do**.

lesson.text: decide, agree, refuse, offer, promise, manage, fail, afford - all take to ... . Contrast them with enjoy, suggest, mind, avoid - which take -ing.

exercises.explanation: agree is followed by to ...: agreed to help him.

exercises.prompt: 'Please don't tell anyone.' 'I won't. I promise.' She promised ___.
exercises.explanation: The negative is not to ...: promised not to tell anyone.

exercises.prompt: There was a lot of traffic, but we managed ___ to the airport in time.
exercises.explanation: manage is followed by to ...: managed to get.

exercises.prompt: I can't play a musical instrument, but I'd like to learn ___ the guitar.
exercises.explanation: learn is followed by to ... (or how to ...): learn to play the guitar.

exercises.prompt: I'm not in a hurry. I don't mind ___.
exercises.explanation: mind is followed by -ing: don't mind waiting.

exercises.prompt: Tina ran in a marathon last week, but she failed ___.
exercises.explanation: fail is followed by to ...: failed to finish.

exercises.statement: We were all afraid to speak. Nobody dared to say anything.
exercises.explanation: Correct. After dare you can use the infinitive with or without to: dared to say / dared say.

exercises.prompt: Tom is worried about something. Say this with appear.
exercises.answer: Tom appears to be worried about something.
exercises.explanation: appear + to be: Tom appears to be worried.

exercises.prompt: They have solved the problem - that is what they say. Say this with claim.
exercises.answer: They claim to have solved the problem.
exercises.explanation: The perfect infinitive to have (done) refers to something already finished: claim to have solved.

exercises.prompt: David is very quiet. He tends not ___ much.
exercises.explanation: tend is followed by to ...; the negative is not to ...: tends not to say much.

exercises.prompt: I've been invited to the party, but I haven't decided ___ or not.
exercises.explanation: decide + question word + to ...: decided whether to go or not.

exercises.prompt: I have some clothes to wash. Can you show me ___ the washing machine?
exercises.explanation: show somebody + how + to ...: show me how to use.
